items.summary: Update the role model to use exactly these roles everywhere the app checks or displays role: `super_admin`, `helper_admin`, `user` (remove/stop using the legacy `admin` role in UI logic and guards).
Enforce admin-route access rules so that only `super_admin` and `helper_admin` can access `/admin/users`, and normal users cannot access any admin routes.

Create/adjust the Admin Users Dashboard at route `/admin/users` to show a **Pending** list that only includes Firestore `users` documents where `approved == false` (do not show already-approved users in this list).

Implement strict field-level visibility on `/admin/users`:
- `super_admin` can see: profile photo, name, age, relation, phone number, email, role, approval status
- `helper_admin` can see ONLY: profile photo, name, age, relation, approval status
- `helper_admin` must not see: phone number, email, role-change options, delete options

Implement admin actions on pending users with strict role separation:
- `super_admin`: Approve user, Reject user, Block user, Promote user to `helper_admin`
- `helper_admin`: Approve user, Reject user
Also ensure the UI does not expose disallowed actions to `helper_admin` and does not allow `helper_admin` to execute role changes or deletion via any client-side path.

Persist approval/rejection/block state in Firestore so login behavior matches requirements:
- On approval: set `approved = true`
- On rejection: keep `approved = false` and store a rejection flag/status so the app can show “Rejected by admin” on login
- On block: store a block flag/status so the app can prevent login access and show an appropriate message
Keep existing signup flow intact (do not change signup logic).

Update the login flow to display the exact message “Rejected by admin” when a user attempts to log in and their Firestore profile indicates they were rejected (while still unapproved). Also prevent blocked users from proceeding past login with a clear English message.

Update Firestore security rules (`frontend/firestore.rules`) to support the new `helper_admin` role:
- Allow `helper_admin` to read the users collection as needed for `/admin/users`
- Allow `helper_admin` to update only the minimal fields needed to approve/reject (and never role/phone/email)
- Keep `super_admin` as the only role that can update roles, delete users, or perform privileged updates
Ensure role privacy in the UI: clearly label roles internally for admins, but do not expose whether any admin is `super_admin` vs `helper_admin` to normal users anywhere in the non-admin UI.
